endpoint.text: Secondary outcomes included changes in metabolic parameters.
Primary outcomes were percentage total weight loss (%TWL) and changes in body mass index (BMI) at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months.
Primary outcomes included percent total weight loss (%TWL) and changes in BMI.

reported_results.text: Mean BMI decreased from 32.7 ± 2.8 to 23.8 ± 2.6 kg/m2 in the SG group and from 32.0 ± 2.6 to 28.4 ± 4.0 kg/m2 in the semaglutide group (p < 0.001).
At 12 months, mean %TWL was 28.6% for SG versus 11.3% for semaglutide (p < 0.001).
Mean BMI decreased from 32.7 ± 2.8 to 23.8 ± 2.6 kg/ m2 in the SG group, compared with a decrease from 32.0 ± 2.6 to 28.4 ± 4.0 kg/m2 in the semaglutide group at 12 months (p < 0.001).
By 6 months, SG patients had maintained a significantly greater weight reduction, with a mean %TWL of 28.6% compared with 11.3% in the semaglutide group (p < 0.001) (Table 3).
At 1 month, the SG group achieved a mean %TWL of 11.1% compared with 6.3% in the semaglutide group (p < 0.001).
A score ≥ 8 was reported in 16 of 36 SG patients (44.4%) compared with 7 of 35 semaglutide patients (20.0%).
